sources.entry: Software and tools to help with resource and supply planning, including enterprise resource and supply planning (ERP).

summary.name: Enterprise resource planning
summary.one_liner: Wikipedia article describing enterprise resource planning (ERP), the category of integrated business management software that covers finance, manufacturing, HR, supply chain and other core business processes.
keywords: running a business with one database
use_cases: understanding what an ERP system covers
learning about ERP customization versus configuration
reviewing ERP modules such as finance and HR
summary.what_it_does: The page is a general encyclopedia overview of enterprise resource planning rather than a single product. It explains that ERP suites integrate business processes such as finance, manufacturing, HR, order processing, supply chain and project management on a shared database. It covers history (the term was credited to Gartner in the 1990s, ERP II in 2000, postmodern ERP in 2013), local versus cloud deployment, and multi-tier deployment. It also discusses implementation, configuration versus customization, and the use of ERP in government.
notable: Describes ERP functional modules such as financial accounting, manufacturing, HR, and supply chain management
Covers the shift from on-premise to cloud ERP and the Gartner 'postmodern ERP' concept
Discusses configuration versus customization trade-offs and typical implementation timelines
caveats: Describes a category of software in general, not one specific product that can be downloaded or used
Page text is cut off before the data migration section; some content may be missing
